{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Replace sentinel value -999.0 in biomarker_baseline with NaN
trial_df['biomarker_baseline'] = trial_df['biomarker_baseline'].replace(-999.0, pd.NA)

# Check for any remaining sentinel values
print("Remaining sentinel values in biomarker_baseline:")
print(trial_df['biomarker_baseline'].unique())

# Check for missing values in baseline and final biomarker
print("\nMissing biomarker_baseline:")
print(trial_df['biomarker_baseline'].isna().sum())

# Now, calculate improvement: final - baseline
# We'll do this only for non-missing baseline values
trial_df['improvement'] = trial_df['biomarker_final'] - trial_df['biomarker_baseline']

# Check how many patients have valid baseline
print("\nNumber of patients with valid baseline biomarker:")
print(trial_df['biomarker_baseline'].notna().sum())

# Now compute average improvement by arm
improvement_by_arm = trial_df.groupby('arm')['improvement'].mean()
print("\nAverage improvement by arm:")
print(improvement_by_arm)

# But wait — we must account for confounding by severity
# Check the imbalance in severity across arms
print("\nSeverity distribution by arm:")
print(pd.crosstab(trial_df['arm'], trial_df['severity']))

# Severity is strongly associated with arm — treatment arm has more severe cases
# So we cannot compare raw improvement across arms

# We need to adjust for severity — stratify by severity
improvement_by_arm_severity = trial_df.groupby(['arm', 'severity'])['improvement'].mean().unstack(level='severity')
print("\nImprovement by arm and severity:")
print(improvement_by_arm_severity)"}
